questions.text: When entering a new group, I quickly establish my role as a leader.
I experience the world as though my emotional volume knob is permanently set several notches above average.
I notice when someone speeds up their speech to get through a point before they can be interrupted.
I trust that the things that truly matter will stay in my mind without a list.
I tend to assert boundaries for the group about what is and isn't acceptable.
I am energized by helping a group articulate its shared vision to stakeholders.
I hold the view that generosity with my time is the highest form of generosity.
I routinely invest in courses, certifications, and credentials that advance my career.
I routinely prioritize my own deadlines over requests that come from others.
I routinely put my health second to the needs of those who depend on me.
The suffering of the people close to me matters a great deal to me.
My inner life has a quality of spaciousness — there's room for emotions without them crowding everything out.
When a conversation stalls, I push it forward with a concrete proposal.
When someone is in pain, I rarely feel a wish to make it better.
I find myself tracking the emotional trajectory of a conversation as it unfolds.
I do not naturally notice who is comfortable and who is uncomfortable in a group.
When I witness something moving, my eyes well up before I've even decided how I feel about it.
I think about backups only when something goes wrong and I wish I had one.
I routinely set aside time and money specifically for my own growth and enjoyment.
I can feel adrenaline surge through me in response to relatively minor provocations.
Once I stop hearing about a person's troubles, I stop thinking about their wellbeing.
Understanding how a policy harms people makes me concerned for them, even if it does not affect me.
I am highly aware of who initiates conversation and who waits to be approached in social settings.
I prefer to dive into a project and let the structure emerge organically.
I would spend my sabbatical working on behalf of a community project rather than resting.
I keep a detailed calendar and refer to it multiple times a day.
I tend to let multiple people contribute to important documents without one person holding the pen.
I tend not to think about why someone chose to sit where they sat.
I notice that I rarely feel the need to talk through my emotions to reduce their intensity.
I keep a master list of all ongoing projects and their current statuses.
I tend to absorb the emotional content of a conversation without it altering my physiological state.
Other people's hardships tend to matter little to me.
I tend to assume people are in a neutral mood unless they tell me otherwise.
When I understand how someone's pain could be eased, I want that relief for them.
I look for ways to distribute ownership of problems across the group.
I think about what skills I'll need in the future and start developing them now.
